symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of scalar latent nodes.

symbols.name: \([n]\)
symbols.def: The labeled latent-node set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The latent causal DAG on \([n]\).

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\)
symbols.def: The parents of node \(i\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: The prescribed signs of the own-coordinate log-ratio derivatives.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The scalar latent causal variables \(V=(V_1,\ldots,V_n)\).

symbols.name: \(p_i\)
symbols.def: The observational conditional density \(p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\).

symbols.name: \(q_i\)
symbols.def: The perfect-intervention density replacing \(p_i\) at target \(i\).

symbols.name: \(Q_i\)
symbols.def: \(Q_i(v)=\int_0^v q_i(u)\,du\).

symbols.name: \(p^0\)
symbols.def: \(p^0(v)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\).

symbols.name: \(p^i\)
symbols.def: \(p^i(v)=q_i(v_i)\prod_{\ell\ne i}p_\ell(v_\ell\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\ell)})\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: The image of the latent cube under the shared mixing map.

symbols.name: f
symbols.def: The shared observation map from latent variables to the observed support.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observation \(X=f(V)\).

symbols.name: \(P^e\)
symbols.def: The pushforward law of \(X\) in observed environment \(e\), with \(e=0\) observational and \(e\in[n]\) interventional after an unknown target relabeling.

symbols.name: \(\pi\)
symbols.def: The unknown bijection from interventional environment labels to latent intervention targets.

symbols.name: \(G^\pi\)
symbols.def: The pullback of \(G\) by \(\pi\), so \(j\to i\) in \(G^\pi\) exactly when \(\pi(j)\to\pi(i)\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: \(R_i\)
symbols.def: \(R_i=dP^i/dP^0\), equal after unmixing to \(q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)})/p_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))})\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The Gaussian kernel \(k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\).

symbols.name: \(D_{ji}\)
symbols.def: \(D_{ji}=\operatorname{MMD}_k(\operatorname{Law}_{P^0}(R_i),\operatorname{Law}_{P^j}(R_i))\) for \(j\ne i\).

symbols.name: \(F_{ji}\)
symbols.def: \(F_{ji}=\mathbb E_{P^j}[R_i^2]-\mathbb E_{P^0}[R_i^2]\) for \(j\ne i\).

symbols.name: \(j\lessdot_G i\)
symbols.def: The relation in which \(j\) is a strict ancestor of \(i\) in \(G\) and no vertex lies strictly between them in the ancestral order.

symbols.name: \(\Theta_{G,s}\)
symbols.def: The causal-minimal positive normalized \(C^3\) mechanism stratum with derivative signs \(s\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\)
symbols.def: The mechanisms with nonzero second-moment contrast on every direct edge.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\)
symbols.def: The mechanisms with positive Gaussian-kernel MMD on every ancestral cover.

symbols.name: \(H_D\)
symbols.space: directed graphs on interventional environment labels
symbols.def: The graph with arrow \(j\to i\) exactly when \(D_{ji}>0\).

symbols.name: \(L_i\)
symbols.def: \(L_i=\log R_i\).

symbols.name: \(B_i\)
symbols.def: The environment labels preceding \(i\) in an arbitrary fixed topological ordering of \(H_D\) selected by the decoder.

symbols.name: \(C_i\)
symbols.def: \(C_i(t\mid\ell_{B_i})=P^i(L_i\le t\mid L_{B_i}=\ell_{B_i})\), using its continuous version on the model support.

symbols.name: \(U_i\)
symbols.def: \(U_i(x)=C_i(L_i(x)\mid L_{B_i}(x))\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr D\)
symbols.def: The ratio-graph, conditional-rank, target-alignment, and parent-pruning decoder.

symbols.name: \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\)
symbols.def: The explicit \(1\to2\) plus isolated-node witness.

symbols.name: \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\)
symbols.def: The explicit faithful mechanism whose direct-edge ratio law is unchanged by intervention on the parent.

symbols.name: \(\theta^t\)
symbols.def: The nodewise normalized affine interpolation from a mechanism to \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\).

symbols.name: \(N_e\)
symbols.def: The number of observations available from environment \(e\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat R_i\)
symbols.def: A density-ratio estimate fitted without the evaluation observations.

symbols.name: \(\widehat U_i\)
symbols.def: A second-stage conditional-CDF estimator evaluated at cross-fitted log-ratio thresholds and conditioning arguments.

symbols.name: \(a_N\)
symbols.def: A deterministic radius for the joint evaluation-law \(L^1\) error of the fitted ratios.

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: The evaluation-fold MMD error probability.

symbols.name: \(\eta\)
symbols.def: The failure probability of the joint ratio-error event.

symbols.name: \(\widehat D_{ji}\)
symbols.def: The norm of the difference of empirical Gaussian-kernel mean embeddings of \(\widehat R_i(X)\) under evaluation samples from environments \(0\) and \(j\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)\)
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)=2\sqrt 2\,a_N+2[1+\sqrt{2\log(n(n+1)/\alpha)}]/\sqrt{\min_e N_e}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat H\)
symbols.space: directed graphs on interventional environment labels
symbols.def: The directed graph selected by positive simultaneous lower confidence bounds for \(D_{ji}\).

symbols.name: \(\beta\)
symbols.def: The Holder smoothness order for the bounded statistical subclass.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: The common density and own-derivative lower margin.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: The common upper bound on mechanism, observed-ratio, mixing-map, inverse-map, and transformed-design regularity.

symbols.name: \(\rho\)
symbols.def: The common distance of the latent preimage of the evaluation domain from the boundary of the latent cube.

symbols.name: \(K\)
symbols.def: The fixed observed-space domain on which every ratio and recovered coordinate is evaluated uniformly.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Z_i(K)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z_i(K)=\{L_{B_i}(x):x\in K\}\).

symbols.name: \(g_i\)
symbols.def: The density of \(L_{B_i}(X)\) under \(P^i\), with \(g_i\equiv1\) when \(B_i=\varnothing\).

symbols.name: \(\underline N\)
symbols.def: \(\underline N=\min_{0\le e\le n}N_e\).

symbols.name: \(d_\star\)
symbols.def: \(d_\star=\max_{i\in[n]}|B_i|\).

symbols.name: \(b_N\)
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences converging to zero
symbols.def: The prescribed simultaneous \(C^1(\mathcal X)\) error rate for the cross-fitted log-ratio estimators.

symbols.name: \(\eta_N\)
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences converging to zero
symbols.def: The failure probability attached to the uniform first-stage ratio contract.

symbols.name: \(h_N\)
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences converging to zero
symbols.def: The common local-linear conditional-CDF bandwidth.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)=\{\max_{i\in[n]}\|\log\widehat R_i-\log R_i\|_{C^1(\mathcal X)}\le b_N\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\)
symbols.def: The bounded Holder subclass with a common interior domain, quantitative mixing geometry, observed-ratio regularity, and transformed-design envelopes.

symbols.name: \(r_N\)
symbols.def: \(r_N=h_N^2+\sqrt{\log(\underline N)/(\underline N h_N^{d_\star})}+b_N/h_N\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\)
symbols.def: The local-linear conditional-CDF and generated-covariate linearization handle.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in[n]\), the mechanism \(p_i\) and intervention density \(q_i\) are strictly positive normalized \(C^3\) densities on their closed cubes.

standard.name: smooth full-support density condition on a compact product support

assumptions.condition: The observational density \(p^0\) is faithful to the DAG \(G\).
The same map \(f\) is a \(C^2\) diffeomorphism of \([0,1]^n\) onto \(\mathcal X\) in every environment.
Besides the known observational law \(P^0\), the laws \(P^1,\ldots,P^n\) arise from distinct unknown targets and replace exactly one \(p_i\) by the corresponding parent-independent density \(q_i\).
For every \(i\in[n]\), \(s_i\,\partial_{v_i}\log\{q_i(v_i)/p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\}>0\) throughout the closed cube.

standard.name: fixed-sign compact-support variant of the everywhere-change condition

assumptions.condition: Within each environment \(e\), the \(N_e\) observations are independent draws from \(P^e\), and the training and evaluation folds are independent.

standard.name: independent multi-sample sampling with sample splitting

assumptions.condition: Every \(p_i\), \(q_i\), and latent-coordinate log-ratio \(L_i\circ f\) has Holder norm of order \(\beta\) at most \(M\).
Every \(p_i\) and \(q_i\) is bounded below by \(c\) on its closed cube.
For every \(i\in[n]\), \(s_i\,\partial_{v_i}L_i(f(v))\ge c\) throughout the closed cube.

novel.justification: This author-imposed strengthening is credible for compact-support exponential tilts and monotone likelihood-ratio mechanisms whose own-coordinate score stays uniformly away from zero. It is confined to the bounded generated-rank subclass and supplies quantitative stability of the inverse rank coordinate on the interior domain.

assumptions.condition: The shared mixing map obeys \(\max\{\|f\|_{C^2([0,1]^n)},\|f^{-1}\|_{C^2(\mathcal X)},\sup_{v\in[0,1]^n}|\det Df(v)|,\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|\det Df^{-1}(x)|\}\le M\).

novel.justification: This author-imposed strengthening is credible for compact-domain bi-Lipschitz \(C^2\) normalizing flows with bounded weights and uniformly conditioned Jacobians. It is confined to the bounded generated-rank subclass and supplies quantitative control of transformed coordinate neighborhoods and their densities.

standard.name: uniformly bounded smooth generated regressors on an interior compactum

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in[n]\), the conditioning-coordinate density obeys \(c\le g_i(z)\le M\) for all \(z\in\mathcal Z_i(K)\).
For every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\), the observational law \(p^0\) does not satisfy \(V_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}V_j\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\setminus\{j\}}\).

standard.name: causal minimality in local edge form under positivity; SpirtesGlymourScheines2000

definitions.name: \(\Theta_{G,s}\)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{G,s}=\{((p_i,q_i))_{i=1}^{n}:\text{ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms, ass:causal-minimality, and ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign hold for }G,s\}\), equipped with the relative product \(C^2\) topology.

definitions.name: \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\)
definitions.construction: On \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated, set \(h(z)=2z-1\), \(q_i(z)=4\exp(4z)/(\exp(4)-1)\), \(p_2(y\mid x)=1+0.1h(x)h(y)\), and \(p_1=p_3=1\); obtain other sign vectors by reflecting each coordinate \(z\mapsto1-z\) when its prescribed sign is negative.

definitions.name: \(\theta^t\)
definitions.construction: For any \(\theta=((p_i,q_i))_{i=1}^{n}\in\Theta_{G,s}\) and a chosen edge \(j\to i\), embed the reflected edge-specific version of \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) in \(G\) and set \(p_\ell^t=(1-t)p_\ell+t p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}\) and \(q_\ell^t=(1-t)q_\ell+t q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}\) for \(t\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\)
definitions.construction: On \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated, set \(q_i(z)=4\exp(4z)/(\exp(4)-1)\), \(p_1=p_3=1\), \(h(y)=2y-1\), \(H(x)=(\exp(4x)-1)/(\exp(4)-1)-x\), and \(p_2(y\mid x)=1+0.1H(x)h(y)\); obtain other sign vectors by coordinate reflections.

definitions.name: \(\mathscr D\)
definitions.construction: From \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), compute every \(R_i\) and \(D_{ji}\), form \(H_D=\{j\to i:D_{ji}>0\}\), select a topological ordering of \(H_D\), construct every coordinate \(U_i=C_i(L_i\mid L_{B_i})\), and align environment \(i\) with \(U_i\). For each \(i\), range over all subsets \(A\subseteq B_i\), evaluate \(U_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}_{P^0}U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A\) under the observational law \(P^0\), and return the environment-label DAG whose parent set at \(i\) is the unique inclusion-minimal subset satisfying this conditional independence.

definitions.name: \(\widehat H\)
definitions.construction: Fit \(\widehat R_i\) on training folds, compute \(\widehat D_{ji}\) on independent evaluation folds, and put \(j\to i\) in \(\widehat H\) exactly when \(\widehat D_{ji}-\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)>0\).

definitions.name: \(\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)=\{\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:\text{ass:bounded-holder-radius, ass:density-lower-envelope, ass:own-derivative-margin, ass:common-interior-domain, ass:bounded-shared-mixing-geometry, ass:observed-log-ratio-regularity, and ass:conditional-design-envelope hold for }n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)=\{\max_{i\in[n]}\|\log\widehat R_i-\log R_i\|_{C^1(\mathcal X)}\le b_N\}\), with the contract \(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}\Pr_\theta\{\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\}\ge1-\eta_N\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\)
definitions.construction: Adapt Xie's local-linear conditional-CDF estimator to cross-fitted log-ratio responses and covariates; decompose the second stage into the oracle conditional-CDF process, indicator boundary crossings from the generated threshold, and local-design perturbations from generated conditioning arguments, then linearize the last component with the generated-covariate expansion of Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle.

statements.statement: The constructions \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) and \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) are positive, normalized, \(C^\infty\), faithful to \(1\to2\) plus isolated node \(3\), and satisfy the prescribed derivative signs after reflection. The sparse witness obeys \(\mathbb E_{P^0}[R_2^2]-\mathbb E_{P^1}[R_2^2]>3\times10^{-4}\) and \(D_{12}>5\times10^{-8}\), whereas the entire direct-edge ratio law under \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) is identical in environments \(0\) and \(1\), so \(D_{12}=0\).
statements.justification: The separating endpoint makes the analytic perturbation nontrivial, while the exact cancellation example shows that cover separation is genuinely generic rather than automatic.
statements.gap: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, equation (3.2)) motivate fine tuning abstractly but do not give this compact-support certified separator and full-law cancellation pair.
statements.consumer: The endpoint and cancellation pair are the bounded early kill test for the open-density theorem.

statements.statement: After the harmless target relabeling \(\pi=\operatorname{id}\), fix \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) and an edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\). Along the path \(\theta^t\), \[F_{ji}(\theta^t)=\int_{[0,1]^n}\frac{(q_i^t)^2(q_j^t-p_j^t)\prod_{\ell\ne i,j}p_\ell^t}{p_i^t}\,dv\] is real analytic on an open interval containing \([0,1]\), is nonzero at \(t=1\), and has isolated zeros. For every relative \(C^2\) neighborhood of \(\theta\), some sufficiently small \(t>0\) remains in \(\Theta_{G,s}\) and satisfies \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)\ne0\).
statements.justification: This is the ratio-specific step that turns one explicit edge witness into density inside every causal-minimal derivative-sign stratum.
statements.gap: Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij (2026, Definition 4 and Lemma 3) preserve Bayesian-network factorization by kernel interpolation, but do not derive analyticity or nonidentity for a surgical density-ratio law.
statements.consumer: A finite iteration of this lemma separates all edges without requiring one distant endpoint to be causal-minimal for the entire DAG.

statements.statement: For every finite labeled DAG \(G\), sign vector \(s\), and target permutation \(\pi\) with \(\Theta_{G,s}\ne\varnothing\), the set \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) is open dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\). Therefore \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) is open dense and residual, and its complement is closed nowhere dense. For the empty graph, both sets equal \(\Theta_{G,s}\).
statements.justification: The theorem derives generic ratio separation from normalized mechanisms; causal minimality keeps every graph edge active and prunes parents in the downstream exact decoder.
statements.gap: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorem 3.2 and equation (3.2)) assume bivariate ratio-law separation; no cited result proves open density of cover separation for every finite DAG and fixed derivative-sign stratum.
statements.consumer: The theorem certifies generic applicability of the population decoder in causal-minimal strata, including disconnected strata with roots, isolates, forks, colliders, redundant ancestral edges, and opposite parent effects.

statements.statement: For every mechanism in \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\), the observed laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\) identify the latent representation and structure via \(\mathscr D\): \(\operatorname{TC}(H_D)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi)\); each \(U_i\) equals \(Q_{\pi(i)}(V_{\pi(i)})\) when \(s_{\pi(i)}=+1\) and \(1-Q_{\pi(i)}(V_{\pi(i)})\) when \(s_{\pi(i)}=-1\); and environment \(i\) is thereby aligned with its recovered coordinate. Every topological ordering of \(H_D\) places the environment-label parent set \(\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i)))\) inside \(B_i\). Under the observational law \(P^0\), for every \(i\in[n]\) and every subset \(A\subseteq B_i\), \[U_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}_{P^0}U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi^{-1}(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i)))\subseteq A.\] Consequently causal minimality makes \(\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i)))\) the unique inclusion-minimal admissible conditioning set, so parent pruning returns exactly \(G^\pi\), independently of the selected topological ordering. Any compatible causal-minimal representation satisfying the same positive normalized scalar perfect-intervention, shared \(C^2\)-mixing, and own-derivative conditions differs only by simultaneous relabeling and componentwise \(C^2\) diffeomorphisms. On the overlapping positive \(C^3\) compact-cube, \(C^2\)-mixing faithful regime, this improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count of von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorem 3.4) from two perfect interventions per node to one. Within the present regime, the decoding and uniqueness conclusions extend structurally from faithful to causal-minimal mechanisms; they do not settle the anchor's full \(\mathbb R^n\), \(C^1\) class. At \(n=2\), Gaussian-MMD positivity supplies the continuous law-separation witness used in their Theorem 3.2. Relative to Wendong et al. (2023, Theorem 4.2) and Yao et al. (2025, Corollary D.1), the decoder recovers rather than takes as given the graph or topological order and intervention alignment.
statements.justification: The observable ratio graph removes the arbitrary-dimensional target-permutation obstacle before conditional ranks recover coordinates and causal minimality prunes parents.
statements.gap: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Section 7) explicitly leave this one-intervention arbitrary-dimensional extension open; CauCA and Yao et al. supply the graph or topological order rather than recovering it. Jiang and Aragam (2023, Theorem 3.4) instead identify a measurement-model graph up to isolated edges from marginal-independence signatures, without recovering an invertibly mixed representation or using a ratio-order certificate. Ahuja et al. (2023, Assumptions 4.1--4.2, Assumption 5.2, and Theorem 5.3) use one unknown-alignment perfect do environment per latent together with finite-degree full-column-rank polynomial mixing and support geometry to identify intervened coordinates up to affine ambiguity; that point-mass support regime is incomparable with positive common-support stochastic interventions under arbitrary shared \(C^2\) diffeomorphic mixing. Buchholz et al. (2023, Assumptions 1--4 and Theorem 1) share unknown single-node intervention targets and arbitrary nonlinear mixing, but require a linear Gaussian latent SCM; the present smooth positive compact-support nonparametric model and observable ratio-order certificate are an incomparable regime rather than a subsumption claim.
statements.consumer: A compliant one-intervention-per-joint ROPES protocol can replace paired acquisition once it uses the ratio decoder and a positive common-support causal generator.

statements.statement: For arbitrary training-fold estimates \(\widehat R_i\), suppose the simultaneous first-stage event \(\{\max_{i,e}\mathbb E_{P^e}|\widehat R_i(X)-R_i(X)|\le a_N\}\) has probability at least \(1-\eta\). Conditional on the training folds and this event, the independent evaluation folds satisfy \[\Pr_{\mathrm{eval}}\!\left\{\max_{j\ne i}|\widehat D_{ji}-D_{ji}|\le\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Consequently the same simultaneous bound has unconditional probability at least \(1-\alpha-\eta\). Every edge of \(\widehat H\) is a true ancestral relation in \(G^\pi\); if \(\min_{\pi(j)\lessdot_G\pi(i)}D_{ji}>2\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)\), then \(\operatorname{TC}(\widehat H)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi)\).
statements.justification: The result separates the verifiable MMD concentration layer from the unresolved construction of a ratio learner with a data-driven radius.
statements.gap: Gretton et al. (2012) study observed MMD inputs, while Acarturk et al. (2024) analyze linear score contrasts rather than shared plug-in likelihood-ratio evaluations across a graph.
statements.consumer: The lower confidence edges give familywise-valid ancestral discoveries and exact order recovery whenever the finite-sample cover margin clears the explicit radius.

statements.statement: Assume the first-stage contract \(\inf_{\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}\Pr_\theta\{\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\}\ge1-\eta_N\), and let \(h_N\to0\) satisfy \(b_N=o(h_N)\) and \(\underline N h_N^{d_\star}/\log(\underline N)\to\infty\). Using the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\), can one construct cross-fitted estimators \(\widehat U_i\) such that \(\max_{i\in[n]}\|\widehat U_i-U_i\|_{\infty,K}=O_{\Pr,\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}(r_N)\), where \(r_N=h_N^2+\sqrt{\log(\underline N)/(\underline N h_N^{d_\star})}+b_N/h_N\)? When the first-stage log-ratio estimators additionally admit a uniform asymptotically linear representation on \(K\), derive the corresponding expansion for \(\widehat U_i-U_i\) that separates threshold crossings, generated-conditioning perturbations, oracle conditional-CDF variance, and smoothing bias, and characterize the weakest sufficient first-stage remainder bound.
statements.justification: The explicit \(C^1(K)\) first-stage contract makes the effects of a generated threshold and generated conditioning neighborhoods quantitatively separable from oracle smoothing error.
statements.gap: Xie (2023, Theorems 1--3) assumes observed thresholds and covariates; Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012, Theorem 1) linearize generated covariates for smooth regression responses, and neither result covers their joint generated-ratio combination.
statements.consumer: A solved expansion supplies coordinate error bars for the one-intervention nonlinear CRL decoder and is the missing statistical ingredient for a compliant ROPES implementation.

sampling_model.design: One known observational environment and one unknown-target stochastic perfect-intervention environment per latent node.
sampling_model.units: Independent observations within each of the \(n+1\) environments, split into ratio-training and evaluation folds.
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(i\) replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a positive parent-independent density; target labels are unknown and distinct.
sampling_model.overlap: All latent observational and interventional densities are strictly positive on the common compact cube.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Density ratios are fitted on training folds. The MMD theorem is conditional on its simultaneous evaluation-law \(L^1\) error event. The generated-rank question is separately conditional on the uniform \(C^1(K)\) log-ratio event \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\), with failure probability at most \(\eta_N\).

target_estimand: \((f^{-1},G,\pi)\) modulo simultaneous relabeling and componentwise \(C^2\) diffeomorphisms

tldr: One unknown-target perfect intervention per latent node generically identifies an arbitrary finite nonlinear causal representation under a shared diffeomorphic mixing. The key object is the observable ratio graph: Gaussian-kernel MMD compares the law of each observational-to-interventional likelihood ratio across environments, and positive discrepancies on ancestral covers recover the transitive closure. Normalized affine interpolation toward a certified sparse edge witness makes this cover condition open dense in every nonempty faithful derivative-sign stratum. Conditional ranks then recover componentwise coordinates and align intervention targets; observational-law conditional independences over subsets of observable-order predecessors have the true parent set as their unique inclusion-minimal solution by faithfulness. A sample-split MMD theorem supplies simultaneous confidence edges conditional on its stated ratio-error event; on a common interior compact domain with bounded mixing geometry, the open statistical question targets an explicit uniform conditional-rank rate under a simultaneous \(C^1\) log-ratio contract.

project_justification.gap: The closest invertible-mixing nonparametric result proves one unknown-target perfect intervention per node only for two latents and explicitly leaves arbitrary dimension open. Jiang and Aragam obtain one-intervention nonparametric latent-graph recovery under measurement-model graphical assumptions. Ahuja et al. obtain one-per-latent perfect-do coordinate recovery from support geometry under finite-degree full-column-rank polynomial mixing, but do not recover the DAG in the arbitrary shared-diffeomorphic positive-density regime. Buchholz et al. obtain arbitrary-dimensional unknown-target single-node recovery under general nonlinear mixing by restricting the latent SCM to linear Gaussian structure, whereas other general-dimensional results double the intervention count, supply the order or graph, or impose additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic latent mechanisms.
project_justification.niche: A mixing-invariant law of observed likelihood ratios can encode ancestry directly on environment labels, avoiding enumeration of target permutations, but its required noncancellation must be derived within normalized faithful mechanism strata rather than assumed.
project_justification.fill: The project proves ratio-specific open density by analytic interpolation, decodes the full causal representation and DAG from the ratio graph and conditional ranks, gives honest conditional confidence edges, and isolates generated-ratio conditional-CDF theory as the remaining first-class open question.

related_work: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4 and Section 7) are the direct invertible-mixing comparator: intervention targets are unknown and neither the graph nor an order is supplied; one perfect stochastic intervention per node identifies the graph and representation only for two latents under a ratio-law witness, while arbitrary dimension uses two distinct paired perfect interventions per node. Their mixing and latent mechanisms are nonparametric. Theorem 2 strictly tightens the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count on the stated open-dense derivative-sign strata and reduces to their bivariate witness logic when \(n=2\). Wendong et al. (2023, Theorem 4.2) use one target-aligned perfect stochastic intervention per node and arbitrary \(C^1\) diffeomorphic mixing with nonparametric mechanisms, but take the full DAG and intervention targets as inputs; they recover components and mechanisms up to componentwise reparametrization. Theorem 2 recovers those supplied structural inputs. Jiang and Aragam (2023, Assumptions 1--2, Theorem 3.4, and Sections 4--5) are an orthogonal comparator: from at most one unknown intervention per hidden variable they recover a maximal latent measurement-model graph, up to isolated latent edges and without knowing the number of hidden variables, under marginal-independence, imaginary-subset, and isolated-edge graphical conditions. They neither assume nor recover coordinates under shared invertible mixing, while the present model does not impose their measurement-DAG conditions; neither result subsumes the other. Ahuja et al. (2023, Assumptions 4.1--4.2, Assumption 5.2, Theorem 5.3, and page 4) identify each intervened latent up to shift and scaling from one point-mass perfect do environment per latent without requiring alignment to a learned coordinate. Their certificate is the support geometry of observational and unintervened latents and requires a finite-degree full-column-rank polynomial decoder and a polynomial learned decoder; it does not recover the causal DAG. The present theorem instead uses positive common-support stochastic interventions, arbitrary shared \(C^2\) diffeomorphic mixing, smooth positive compact-support nonparametric mechanisms, and a ratio-order certificate that recovers both alignment and the graph. These assumptions are orthogonal, so no subsumption is claimed. Buchholz et al. (2023, Assumptions 1--4 and Theorem 1) share unknown single-node perfect-intervention targets, no supplied graph or order, and arbitrary nonlinear mixing, and recover the full latent model, targets, and graph up to permutation and scaling. Their latent SCM is linear Gaussian and their proof uses precision-matrix quadratic geometry; the present smooth positive compact-support nonparametric mechanisms and ratio-order certificate define an incomparable regime. Yao et al. (2025, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1) use one single-node environment per latent within a smooth-invertible invariance framework, but supply a topological intervention-target order and recover elementwise components rather than the order itself; Theorem 2 recovers that order. Var\i{}c\i{} et al. (2025, Theorem 29) are informed-by prior art for unknown-target score-change recovery under general transformations with two uncoupled hard interventions per node. Ng et al. (2025, Theorems 1--2) use nonparametric mixing and no supplied order, but replace per-node intervention coverage by derivative-rich general environments and restrict latent mechanisms to additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic families. Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij (2026, Definition 4 and Lemmas 3--4) supply normalized conditional-kernel interpolation and faithfulness topology for a fixed DAG, not a mixed representation or intervention assignment; the surgical-ratio analytic contrast is new work. Gretton et al. (2012, Theorems 5, 7, and 13) supply characteristicness and MMD concentration for directly observed two-sample inputs, not plug-in ratio graphs. Xie (2023, Theorems 1--3) and Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012, Theorem 1) supply complementary observed-argument and generated-covariate pieces of the unresolved generated-rank expansion. Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026, Theorems 4.6--4.7) give finite-sample decoder and graph recovery under high-dimensional linear factor mixing and unknown multi-node interventions, a different statistical regime.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact cancellation mechanism \(H'(x)=q_1(x)-1\) is faithful and sign-valid yet has \(D_{12}=0\), so faithfulness and monotone interventions alone do not imply ratio separation. The genericity theorem supplies no uniform positive MMD margin. Cover margins also do not control exact-parent uncertainty: an arbitrarily weak shortcut edge can be added to a chain while cover discrepancies remain separated.
honest_scope: The population open-density and exact-decoder claims are the primary results. The all-DAG existence argument may use a terminating certified search rather than a closed-form family. The fixed-bandwidth MMD statement remains conditional on its simultaneous first-stage \(L^1\) ratio-error event and does not claim a data-driven radius. The uniform own-derivative margin and quantitatively bounded shared-mixing geometry are author-imposed strengthenings not supplied by von Kugelgen et al. (2023); both are confined to \(\texttt{def:bounded-holder-subclass}\) and \(\texttt{oeq:generated-rank-frontier}\) and do not enter the population genericity or exact-decoder claims. Attainment and sharpness of the stated generated-rank rate under the uniform \(C^1(K)\) first-stage contract, and the additional first-stage representation needed for a uniform asymptotically linear expansion, remain open. Exact-parent inference under a separate conditional-dependence margin, noncompact supports, vector-valued nodes, imperfect interventions, and noninvertible observations remain outside the settled core. The \(n=2\) reduction recovers the witness-function logic of von Kugelgen et al. (2023, Theorem 3.2). ROPES is a consumer only after adopting a positive common-support generator and a ratio-based estimator; its current bounded additive-noise causal benchmark is not asserted to satisfy this model.
